guard: both OpenCode plugins hand a once task over at most once: the drive claims it right before the submission, releases it when the submission fails or a turn ended before its answer, and the 1.x plugin's teardown is the exit a once seat takes on its own
why: M1 and M3 drop the release from a failed submission. The task stays claimed, so it is neither
sealed nor reported, and the manager learns nothing until the handoff timer fires.
M2 drops the 1.x claim. The release then seals nothing, the task stays offerable, and the error
retry sends it a second time: the duplicate run this feature exists to prevent.
M4 drops the 2.x claim. A native prompt typed while the submission is in flight peeks the task as
still pending and carries it too.
M5 drops the 1.x exit registration, so a once seat whose report cannot land has no teardown to run.
M6 and M12 confirm a task whose turn ended before the submission's answer, so the next turn's
end yields it as done. M7 notes the 1.x idle only after its position read, which an answer can
overtake. M8 and M9 miss the end an idle status or an error reports. M10 counts the ends from
before the send, so a stale end seals a task that was delivered. M11 drops the 2.x exit
registration, as M5 does for 1.x. M13 confirms a 1.x task whose session was replaced while its
answer was held, and M14 lets a 2.x end with no log position pass unnoticed.
